bio: Kevin Liu is an infra-product engineer in San Francisco and a student at Princeton University who designs interfaces that feel alive.
description: Kevin Liu's projects as 26 collectible cards: type, games, shaders, agents and interfaces, each with its real product, its features as moves, and a battle you can play.
about: I am an infra-product engineer at [General Translation](https://generaltranslation.com) based in San Francisco.
I am 19, and I've been coding and designing since I was 12. I am currently attending [Princeton University](https://www.princeton.edu).

I design interfaces that feel alive, from first principles, with a spirit of their own. I follow friction toward what is missing, and treat environments as part of the product. I build strange observations into useful worlds through type, skills, and protocols.
facts: Kevin Liu is an infra-product engineer at General Translation in San Francisco, since July 2026.
He studies computer science at Princeton University (B.S.E., class of 2028).
He has been coding and designing since he was 12.
Before General Translation he was a founding engineer at Dedalus Labs (January to July 2026), where he built agent infrastructure, and at Sevenfold AI (June to November 2025).
He interned at Amazon (2025), Bloomberg (2023 and 2024) and AT&T Labs Research (2023).
He co-founded the Online Monmouth Math Competition (OMMC), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit math contest, and leads its technology.
He was lead developer of HackPrinceton's websites and built Podium, its judging tool.
He won 13 hackathons in a row; his team's RecyclAIble took first place in hardware at PennApps XXIII (2022).

He is the author of a paper on speech transcription for Huntington's disease (IYRC 2023), which won a Sigma Xi award, and a co-author of a paper on heat flow in lithium-ion polymer batteries (IEEE MIT URTC 2024).
